sections.h: Signs your home may need a rewire
sections.html:
• Old rubber, fabric or lead-sheathed cables
  • An old fuse box with rewireable fuses and no RCD protection
  • Scorch marks, warm sockets, a burning smell or lights that flicker
  • Not enough sockets, with extension leads everywhere
  • An EICR that has come back “unsatisfactory”
  • You’re about to renovate, extend or refit a kitchen — the best time to rewire is before the plastering and decorating

1. Survey and written quote. We look at the property, talk through where you want sockets, lighting and switches, and give you a clear scope of work and price.
  2. First fix. New cables are run and back boxes fitted, usually with floorboards lifted and walls chased. This is the disruptive part, so we plan it around you.
  3. Making good. Walls are then plastered — by your plasterer or builder, or we can recommend one.
  4. Second fix. Sockets, switches, lights and a new consumer unit are fitted and connected.
  5. Testing and certification. The whole installation is tested, you receive an Electrical Installation Certificate, and notifiable work is signed off with Building Control.

sections.h: How long does a rewire take?
sections.html:
It depends on the size of the property, access and whether the house is empty. As a rough guide, a typical three-bedroom house takes around one to two weeks. We’ll give you a realistic timescale with your quote.

It is possible to live in the house during a rewire — we can work room by room and keep power on overnight — but it is quicker and less disruptive if the house is empty or mid-renovation.

Not every home needs a full rewire. If the wiring is sound in most of the house, we can rewire individual rooms or circuits — for example a kitchen, extension or loft — and upgrade the consumer unit at the same time.

faq.q: How much does a rewire cost in Cardiff?
faq.a: It depends on the size of the property, how many sockets and lights you want, and access. We'll visit and give you a fixed written quote so you know exactly what's included before any work starts.

faq.q: Do I need to move out during a rewire?
faq.a: Not usually. We can work room by room and keep power on in the evenings. An empty house is quicker, so if you're renovating anyway it's the ideal time.
Yes. You'll get an Electrical Installation Certificate and notifiable work is signed off with Building Control, which you'll need when you sell the house.

faq.q: Can you work with my builder or plasterer?
faq.a: Yes. We regularly work alongside builders and plasterers and fit our first and second fix around their programme.

title: Consumer Unit & Fuse Box Upgrades in Cardiff | Bailey Electrical
description: Fuse box and consumer unit replacements in Cardiff. Modern metal consumer units with RCD/RCBO protection, tested and certified. Fully insured. Call 07590 275205.
h1: Consumer unit & fuse box upgrades in Cardiff
lead: Replace an old fuse box with a modern consumer unit that protects your family and meets current wiring regulations.
image_alt: Kitchen with under-cabinet LED lighting and downlights

sections.html:
The consumer unit (often called the fuse box) is what protects the circuits in your home. Older boards often have rewireable fuses and no RCD protection, which means they won’t cut the power quickly enough if someone touches a live part.

A modern consumer unit gives you:

  • RCD or RCBO protection on your circuits, designed to protect people from electric shock
  • A non-combustible (metal) enclosure, as required for homes under current regulations
  • Surge protection where the regulations call for it
  • Clearly labelled circuits, so it’s easy to see what’s what

Most consumer unit replacements are done in a day, with the power off for part of it. Before connecting the new board we test the existing circuits: an RCD will trip if there are hidden faults, so any problems we find are explained to you before we go any further.

When the job is finished you get an Electrical Installation Certificate and notifiable work is signed off with Building Control.

• Before or during a renovation, extension or kitchen refit
  • When an EICR has recommended it
  • When you’re adding new circuits, such as an extension, garden office or outdoor lighting
  • When you’ve bought an older property and don’t know the history of the electrics

faq.q: How long does a consumer unit replacement take?
faq.a: Usually a day, depending on the number of circuits and whether any faults are found when the existing wiring is tested.

faq.q: Do I need a new consumer unit?
faq.a: If you still have an old fuse box with rewireable fuses, no RCD protection or a plastic enclosure, it's worth upgrading. We can check it and advise honestly.

faq.q: Will the power be off all day?
faq.a: The power is off for part of the job while the new board is fitted and tested. We'll let you know what to expect beforehand.

sections.h: What we do on renovation projects
sections.html:
• Extensions and loft conversions — new circuits, sockets, lighting and heating controls
  • Kitchens — cooker and appliance circuits, island power, downlights, under-cabinet and plinth lighting
  • Bathrooms — LED mirrors, shower and feature lighting, extractor fans, electric towel rails and underfloor heating, installed to bathroom zone rules
  • Whole-house refurbishments — often combined with a rewire and consumer unit upgrade
  • Outdoor — garden, patio and step lighting and outdoor sockets

On a renovation, timing matters. We do the first fix (cables and back boxes) before plasterboard and plastering, and come back for the second fix (sockets, switches and lights) once decorating is done. We’ll agree the dates with you or your builder so we’re never the trade holding the job up.

It’s much cheaper to put a socket or light in the right place at first fix than to move it later. Before we start we’ll walk through the space with you and think about:

  • Where furniture, the TV and appliances will go
  • Enough sockets, including USB sockets where useful
  • Lighting in layers — general downlights, task lighting and feature lighting
  • Two-way switching and dimmers in the right places
  • Outdoor lighting and power if the extension opens onto the garden

New circuits and most renovation electrical work are notifiable under the Building Regulations. We test everything, issue an Electrical Installation Certificate and make sure notifiable work is signed off with Building Control, so your paperwork is in order for sign-off and when you come to sell.

faq.q: Can you work with my builder?
faq.a: Yes. We work alongside builders, kitchen and bathroom fitters and carpenters, and plan first and second fix around their programme.

faq.q: When should I book an electrician for an extension?
faq.a: As early as possible — ideally when the builder is booked — so first fix can be scheduled before plasterboard goes up.

faq.q: Do you handle Building Regulations for the electrics?
faq.a: Yes. We test and certify the work and make sure it's signed off with Building Control.

h1: EICRs & landlord electrical certificates in Cardiff
lead: Electrical Installation Condition Reports for landlords, letting agents, homebuyers and homeowners — with clear explanations and any remedial work done properly.
image_alt: Bathroom with backlit LED mirror and shower lighting

sections.html: An Electrical Installation Condition Report (EICR) is a detailed inspection and test of a property’s fixed electrical installation — the wiring, consumer unit, sockets, switches and light fittings. It shows whether the installation is safe to keep using and highlights anything that needs attention.

Under the Renting Homes (Wales) rules, landlords must make sure the electrical installation is tested at least every five years and give the contract-holder a copy of the report within 14 days of the occupation contract starting. We carry out EICRs for landlords and letting agents across Cardiff and can quote for and complete any remedial work so the property passes.

• C1 – Danger present. Immediate action needed.
  • C2 – Potentially dangerous. Urgent remedial work needed.
  • C3 – Improvement recommended. Not a fail, but worth considering.
  • FI – Further investigation needed without delay.

Any C1, C2 or FI means the report is “unsatisfactory”. We’ll explain in plain English what was found and what it will cost to put right.

For owner-occupied homes, an EICR is generally recommended every ten years, when you buy a property, or before starting a renovation. It’s a good way to find out whether you need a rewire or consumer unit upgrade before planning other work.

faq.q: How often do landlords in Wales need an EICR?
faq.a: At least every five years, and the contract-holder must be given a copy within 14 days of the occupation contract starting.

faq.q: How long does an EICR take?
faq.a: Typically a few hours for a flat or average-sized house, depending on the number of circuits and access.

faq.q: What happens if the report is unsatisfactory?
faq.a: We'll explain what was found and quote for the remedial work. Once it's done, you'll receive confirmation that the issues have been put right.
